terms.comment: Greek διάκονος, a servant. The Vulgate also has a third-declension plural, diāconibus (Phil. 1.1); Egeria writes diācones. In both churches the deacon reads the Gospel, leads the prayers of the people and censes.
Properly a Levite of the Old Testament; Prudentius gives the name to the deacons Lawrence and Vincent.

phrases.latin: Paulus et Tīmotheus, servī Jēsū Chrīstī, omnibus sānctīs in Chrīstō Jēsū, quī sunt Philippīs, cum episcopīs et diāconibus.
phrases.english: Paul and Timothy, servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are at Philippi, with the bishops and deacons.

phrases.latin: et ūnus ex diāconibus facit commemorātiōnem singulōrum, sīcut solet esse cōnsuētūdō
phrases.english: and one of the deacons makes the commemoration of each person, as the custom is

sources: Lewis & Short: diaconus · Lewis & Short: Levites
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. deacon.
